Meet the First-Ever BMW X5 M Electric!
16 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
It’s been a few months since BMW pulled the wraps off the all-new fifth-generation X5 . The G65, or the G78 as you likely know the LWB (long wheelbase) model if you live in China, debuted back in June, 2026, and two months later, it hit the assembly line at the Spartanburg factory in South Carolina, USA, and at Dadong in the People’s Republic.
It’s not only the regular ICE model that debuted back then, but also the first fully electric X5. It is called the BMW iX5, to no one’s surprise, and unlike its internal combustion-powered sibling, it misses out on the air intakes between the license plate and kidney grille. During the grand unveiling, the company estimated an EPA range of 435 miles (700 km) with the 144 kWh battery pack fully charged.
BMW’s iX5 is officially coming to our market in 2027, the brand’s website reveals, and it packs quite a punch in the 60 AWD configuration. This model has a pair of electric motors that churn out a total of 570 horsepower (578 ps/425 kW) and 593 pound-feet (804 Nm) of torque. The BMW iX5 60 AWD takes only 4.4 seconds from 0-60 mph (0-97 kph). That’s 0.7 seconds slower than the old X5 M, which has 617 hp (625 ps/460 kW) and 553 lb-ft (750 Nm) of torque to play with from its twin-turbo 4.4-liter V8 engine.
As you likely know by now, an entirely new BMW X5 M, based on the G65 generation, is in the making as we speak. Word on the street is that it might pack the same powertrain as the latest M5, namely a plug-in hybrid 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8, which churns out a maximum of 717 hp (727 ps/535 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque in the business super sedan and wagon. The former takes 3.4 seconds from 0 to 62 mph (0-100 kph), and the latter does it in 3.5 seconds.
Photo: SH Proshots Due to the extra weight, because the future BMW X5 M will be heavier, not to mention more spacious, this model is expected to be a bit slower than the latest M5. You know, just like the current M5 is slower than its predecessor. And it will probably not be able to match the straight-line performance of the old X5 M.
And if the ICE BMW X5 M is not exactly to your liking, then you should know that the company is also preparing a battery-electric alternative to this model. The zero-emission X5 M has been caught testing on a few occasions, and it is now back under the limelight, courtesy of our man with the cam, who recently sent the images shared above in the gallery to our inboxes.
Word on the street is that the BMW X5 M Electric , or the iX5 M, whatever it will be named, might have in the region of 800 to 900 brake horsepower to play with. This equals 811-912 metric horsepower, and 596-671 kilowatts. Keep in mind that these numbers are not official, as nobody who is not directly involved in its development knows anything about the powertrain for now.
Photo: SH Proshots As far as the visual differences go, the scooped prototype featured an entirely new bumper with redesigned air intakes. The styling is visible even from beneath the trippy vinyl stickers. The grille appears to be new as well, and chances are that the headlights might feature fresh graphics. The wheel arches do not seem to be on the fat side of things, and from what we can tell, the side skirts do not look different either.
The same goes for the door mirrors, too, though you may want to keep in mind the fact that this is a tester, and these things could change once the model hits the assembly line. The rear bumper is also new, and you should ignore the reflectors, which are provisional. The wheels are also exclusive to the BMW X5 M Electric (or iX5 M), and they should hide an uprated braking system behind them. The chassis setup is likely different, too, as this model should be able to corner faster, while also sitting a bit closer to the ground.
It looks like the fully electric BMW X5 M might come out sometime next year or maybe in 2028, as rumor has it that it could hit the assembly line in the latter year. That is also when its ICE-powered sibling might also come out of hiding, though to be honest, we wouldn’t be surprised if the automaker decides to unveil them a bit sooner.
What’s your take on the first-ever BMW X5 M Electric? Could this model convince you to spend your hard-earned money on it? Tell us all about it in the comments area below, and don’t forget to check it out in more detail in the photo gallery above.
